q: One Christmas, Ricky's present to his sister was...
a: A bottle of shampoo he found in the bathroom and wrapped up
f: His sister had got him a Cat Stevens album, a birdhouse and a quiz book. Ricky was about twelve or thirteen.
ex: ...I think a, a, a birdhouse, er, and, like, a quiz book...
...or something. And, it was my turn to give her her present, and it was a bottle of shampoo that I'd found in the bathroom and wrapped up.
It was a big, jumbo, one of those Tescos, you know...
Had it not already been used?

q: What was the name of Ricky's old chat show, which he reminisced about on XFM?
a: Meet Ricky Gervais
f: Steve, who worked on it, claimed no-one watched it. Karl said he loved it.
ex: Right, no I'm gonna interview Steve, cos you know I used to be a chat show host, well I am a chat show host.
Well, did you see Meet Ricky Gervais?
No... I worked on it and I didn't watch it. No-one watched it.

q: Steve said that Ricky, puffing on a Montecristo cigar weeks before his charity boxing match, looked like who?
a: George Peppard from the A-Team
f: Steve: "It was pathetic. And he was drinking Guinness." Ricky's defence: "I haven't started training yet, I'm starting training next week."
ex: OK. Anyway I was chatting to him last night in the pub cos the boxing match is obviously in about five weeks time I think isn’t it, and anyway... He was sat there, Karl, I don’t know if you know this about Ricky but he’s taken to smoking…
No I have the occasional one..

He got a cigar, he got like a Montecristo out of his pocket, it was ludicrous. He looked like George Peppard, from the A-Team or something. It was pathetic. And he was drinking Guinness, and I was saying to him – aren’t you doing a boxing…
I haven’t started training yet, I’m starting training next week.

q: Explaining amateur versus professional boxing rules, what did Ricky say he'd quite like to ask for in his charity fight?
a: To fight bare-chested so he could show off his body
x: To wear his old karate belt in the ring
To smoke a cigar between rounds
To have Karl as his cornerman
f: Ricky: "Maybe I could ask to fight bare-chested cos I'd quite like to show off my body." Steve: "I think wrestling is probably better for you."
ex: So there’s no title here is there?

No, I mean amateur is head guards, vest, and 16 oz gloves or something. As opposed to professional which is no vest – bare-chested, oh! Maybe I could ask to fight bare-chested cos I’d quite like to show off my body, if I could.
I think wrestling is probably better for you.
But I don’t mean those kinda like - the Rock and people like that I’m talking about Big Daddy – that kind of, where you can just throw yourself at someone.

q: Ricky suggested getting a triple tandem for their roadshow. How would the riding be shared out?
a: Karl does all the pedalling, Ricky sits in a basket at the front

Karl pedals, Ricky rides in a sidecar
Ricky pedals, Karl sits in the basket

ex: Yeah. No I think the pogo stick. The triple tandem.
We should get that, for when we do our roadshow. Karl does all the peddaling. I’m in a basket in the front.

q: Mocking the Rockbusters prizes, Ricky threw in a solo album by Tony Banks of Genesis. What was it called?
a: 'Bankstatement'

ex: And Tony Banks’ own solo album ‘Bankstatement’.
Tony Banks remember is the, er, musician from the much loved Genesis, but we’ve got that album to give away.

q: Karl's Rockbusters clue "At the moment I'm in a river full of logs" meant Justin Timberlake. What annoyed Ricky about it?
a: Karl said river when the answer needed a lake
x: Logs float, so you'd be on them, not in them
Karl had used the same clue the week before

ex: Justin Timberlake. Ah, we had some wrong answers that included Jethro Tull and James Taylor.
I don’t know how that relates to it at all.
I’m annoyed at lake, when he clearly said river.
Steve starts chuckling the more Ricky speaks

I mean that’s the first thing that cropped up Not ‘I’m in some water full of logs,’ ‘At the moment…’ yeah, ‘I’m in some water full of logs,’ but he actually had to say river, so not lake. That annoys me. I mean I didn’t get it, fair…

q: With Karl ignoring the banter because he wanted to finish the show, what did Ricky compare him to?
a: A cat looking through a window at a dead mouse
x: A dog waiting by the door for walkies
A kid staring at the clock on the last day of term
A horse that can smell its stable
f: Ricky: "You wanna press the buttons and finish don't ya." Karl: "Yep." The show ended with "It's ads and that's it."
ex: We were doing humour, we were doing a little bit of humour. It was a satire on you saying age is not being specific, and did – did you like that stuff we do?

Just like a cat looking at a window at a dead mouse or something. He can’t – you can go “Come here!” and it’s just looking at the mouse it could eat. You – you wanna press the buttons and finish don’t ya.
What you gonna do, play a record or…
No, that’s it. It’s ads and that’s it.

q: Ricky's mate was so scared at a West End alien attraction that he did what?
a: Ripped a bit of the foam alien's face off
x: Ran out through the fire exit
f: "It was foam, and the bloke went 'Don't do that, mate'."
ex: Quick, oh yeah, my mate went to one of those things, erm erm, in the West End where it's aliens, and they jump out at you, and he was so scared, that when it jumped out, he ripped a bit of it's face off.
Yeah, it was foam, and the bloke went "Don't do that, mate".

q: Steve mocked Ricky for voicing a drink driving campaign. How did Ricky say he followed the advert's advice?
a: It said don't drink and drive, so he's chosen just to drink
x: He only drinks on the bus home
He drives, but only to the offy
He gave his car keys to Karl
f: Ricky admitted he doesn't even drive, and wasn't sure he'd been paid for it: "Or did I? I can't remember."
ex: Yeah, okay Rick, yeah. You are the voice of what, the drink driving campaign?
You sound, you sound like a man who was run over in a drink driving accident.
I mean it's like, you don't drive-
Yeah but I didn't make any money from that did I?
Or did I? I can't remember. Yeah

q: Defending the show's bronze Sony award, why did Ricky claim bronze is actually better than gold?
a: Gold's got no intrinsic value, it's just a currency
x: Bronze goes better with his complexion
Gold medals are only chocolate inside
f: Steve reminded everyone the bronze Sony was "one of the most coveted of the awards."
ex: It did win a bronze award at the Sony's last year.
One of the most coveted of the awards.
In my- in my opinion the bronze is slightly better than the gold.
Well, a lot of people don't win the bronze, Rick. You gotta remember that- that there's not many people winning...
You see gold is- ya know- gold's got no intrinsic value it's just a currency. In my opinion bronze is better.

q: What did Jane say when she walked past and saw Ricky eating chicken legs in the bath?
a: "Christ! Caligula."
f: Ricky saw himself as "a fat, Roman emperor", but Steve wasn't having it: "Caligula, to be honest, is just too cool and impressive."
ex: I do, I do eat in the bath. I mean, I-I- the second week of doing it, I was just eating in the bath. I was eating- I think I was eating chicken legs again. I’m eating in the bath. Jane walked past. Just looked in at me and she went…
Just me, a fat, Roman emperor eating--
Caligula, to be honest, is just too cool and impressive. You’re not Caligula. Old Man Steptoe.

q: A listener wanted them to talk about art. What did Ricky have to say to Tracey Emin?
a: "Make your bed!"
f: Ricky's entire art discussion: "Make your bed! Damien Hirst! Stop cutting up sharks an' things. Um, Picasso...alright?"
ex: Right. Okay, then. What should we talk about, then? Um....Tracy--
Right, play a record and we’ll discuss this.
Tracey Emin! Sh- make your bed!
Make your bed! (giggles) Damien Hirst! Stop cutting up sharks an’ things. Um, Picasso...alright?

q: Which digital radio station for the over-fifties did Ricky admit he'd been enjoying?
a: SAGA Radio
f: It played Cliff Richard, Sammy Davis Jr. and Here Comes The Sun, "and I was loving it." Steve: "Well, it's aimed at your age group."
ex: Um, I listen to SAGA Radio now sometimes.
It's on digital- I think it's--
And it plays all- it was Cli- it was playing Cliff Richards this morning, it played, um, Sammy Davis Jr., it played, um, Beatles - Here Comes The Sun, and I was loving it.

q: After Karl's tongue-flicking boast, Ricky asked how many he could do if he had to touch Ricky's nipple at the end. What sum did Ricky shout?

ex: I did 148 last night, in a minute. Right?
Play a record! Oh, well hold on, there's my nipple. How many could you do if it meant you had to touch me nipple at the end. £2,000!

q: Ricky joked that Karl wanted which famous mind-reader brought in, because "he won't be able to read me mind", adding that Karl was the one person who could outwit him?
a: Derren Brown
f: Ricky's take on guessing Karl's quiz answers: "when you're trying to guess what's in Karl's mind, you can only get so close."
ex: Okay, you know- if they know what it is cause tha-that’ll stop any ambiguity, won’t it? Um, and, uh, don’t worry if you haven’t got all of them because the winner last week didn’t have all of them, but it’s the-the closest one. I…
Do you know what I mean? He’s-he wants us to bring in Derren Brown. He go, “Cause he won’t be able to read me mind.”
I think he’s the one person that could outwit Derren Brown.

q: Ricky played 'Jessie's Girl' by Rick Springfield but said it had one of the worst lyrics. Which phrase did he mean?
a: "The point may be moot"
f: Steve was appalled: "You don't use that in a rock song!"
ex: Um. And it's got- it's got Kiss, Judas Priest, Deep Purple, The Darkness. I mean, it really is good. It's all it's all your classic, rock tracks. The other reason I wanted to play it is because I like that song, I think it's a great little…
You don't use that in a rock song!

q: Ricky found out that cinemas across America banned popcorn during Schindler's List. Why did that annoy him?
a: It meant eating through every other film was fine
x: He'd planned to take a family bucket
They still let people eat hot dogs
Popcorn should only be banned in comedies
f: The ban was "out of respect to the film". Ricky's solution: "Ban it through all films!"
ex: You know what? Right. What annoyed me is I found out in across America, when they showed Schindler's List, they banned popcorn, right? Out of respect to the film. What?! So they're saying all the other films, oh sod it, doesn't matter. Oh…
I mean, ban it through all films!

q: Why did Ricky say his dad buried a cooker, a fridge and a freezer at the bottom of the garden?
a: The council charged about five quid to take them away
x: He was building a nuclear bunker
To hide them from the bailiffs
He thought they might grow back
f: Also down there: "a dog and a couple of cats—they were dead, to be fair." Steve claimed his own mean dad did the same with dead relatives.
ex: It’s a problem, though, innit, ‘cause you can’t just…
I don’t know what you’re meant to do.

Well listen, right, when I was growing up I remember the council used to charge five pounds or summat to take away, like, cookers and fridges, so my dad used to bury them. Down the bottom of my garden, I don’t know wh—there’s, there’s a…
I’m not saying—I mean, my father’s quite a mean man, as you know… but he, my dad used to do that with dead relatives.

q: The feng shui book said to make a 'wealth vase' of gold, crystal or glass. What was Ricky's objection?
a: If you've got a gold vase you're probably alright for money anyway
x: Gold vases clash with three-legged frogs
Nobody keeps a vase in a cupboard
f: You then fill it with semi-precious stones and "soil taken from a rich man's garden." Steve: "So just find the soil of a rich man."
ex: Ah… the wealth vase, “Make a wealth vase and keep it hidden in your cupboard. It can be made of gold, crystal or gla--,” if, I, can I just say summat, if you’ve got a vase made of gold, you’re probably alright for money anyway.
But this is the wealth vase, how do you make the wealth vase?
“Fill it with semi-precious stones and with soil taken from a rich man’s garden.”
So just find the soil of a rich man.

q: Which Halloween decorations did Ricky object to on a little bakery in Soho?
a: Cobwebs all over it and spiders on the buns
x: Fake blood on the cream cakes
f: Ricky: "even though it's fake... I don't think you should do it on a bakery." He said it "surely puts you off the product a little bit."
ex: Yeah, we can sell stuff and, and film and, and things that are and. But out there, they start, like weeks and weeks before and they're decorated, like, proper proper. But I saw a baker's, a little bakery in Soho, and it didn't look right…
That surely puts you off the product a little bit.

q: A Virgin Radio quiz said the sun is four times bigger than the moon. When a listener emailed '400 times', what was Ricky's theory about the DJ?
a: He assumed 400 was a printing error
x: He'd mixed up the sun and the moon
He was reading the answers upside down
He wanted the woman to win the trip
f: Ricky's version of the DJ: "Nothing can be 400 times bigger than the moon!"
ex: …that go on—I know, but… uhm someone just emailed in saying the sun is indeed about 400 times bigger than the moon, thanks for that. That, that DJ must’ve looked it up and said, “Uhm, 400 times, that can’t be right, it’s probably, they…
“Nothing can be 400 times bigger than the moon!”

q: At The Fat Duck in Bray, voted best restaurant in the world, what did they put in fussy Ricky's version of the snail porridge?
a: Mushrooms
f: Ricky ate before he went, just in case, but said "they really accommodated me." On the way, Jonathan Ross phoned him: "Why are we taking you to this restaurant?"
ex: And uh, uh, me and Jane went along with him and Jane to The Fat Duck in Bray. It was voted the best restaurant in the world.

Okay. And um, it was incredible. I mean, it's a cross between a restaurant and sort of barnum. They take you, just, incredible, but all the way there, I'm thinking well I, I, I can't eat stuff in normal restaurants. I can't eat, I don't…
I, it was, I knew that one of their, um, signature dishes was snail porridge. So I'm thinking "I'm not gonna be able to eat anything here." So I'm thinking I had something to eat before I went.

I was thinking that they better not have mucked around the bread, right? Got there. Beautiful. Um, and uh, it was, it was, it was really quite fantastic. And, and I let them know straight away, um, that I was a philistine and they really…

They put um, mushrooms in my snail porridge, which was more risotto, and its tasting menus and that, and it was, it was, um, uh, really fantastic. But, Jonathan halfway through on the way there, I don't like travel well, on the way there…

q: Filling in for Jonathan Ross on Radio 2, Ricky said he felt like what?
a: A step-father
f: He wanted to tell listeners "I'll never replace Daddy", but also: "Listen, I'm doing mummy now. Live with it."
ex: And uh, Karl Pilkington. If you have tuned in to hear Jonathan, it's the last time I’ll mention him, we haven't got him today. You've got us for the next couple of Saturdays. I feel like a step-father.
You know what I mean? I want to say to the listener. “You know, I’ll never replace Daddy.”
“But I am here and I, and I’ll do my best for you and I love you.”
On the other hand I want to go, “Listen, I'm doing mummy now. Live with it.”

q: Ricky said he'd never put his jumper in the washing machine. When Steve asked what the problem was with a hot wash, what did Ricky warn?
a: It can cause shrinkage
x: It makes the wool go bobbly
f: Ricky recommends "a cold wa- soak", then leaving it out on a few towels or over the radiator. "It can cause shrinkage" became a running joke for the rest of the show.
ex: And then clean it, not in the err washing machine though.
I’d pop it in a cold wa- soak.
And then leave it out on a few towels or summat, or put it over the radiator.
So what's the problem with err, putting it in a hot wash?

q: A newspaper journalist asked whether they liked Karl. What did Ricky say having Karl on the show was like?
a: Having a new kitten he can't wait to see on Saturdays
x: Owning a goldfish that keeps surprising him
Having a pet tortoise that won't come out
f: Ricky told the bloke from the Standard: "I can't wait to get in and see his little face. On Saturdays."
ex: In fact, we did an interview yesterday with a bloke from the Standard, who really liked the show, and said, "Do you like Karl? ‘Cause you take the piss out of him a lot." And we’d just like to say, we LOVE Karl. I said, to that bloke…

q: Steve spotted a TV show called "I Survived a 200 Pound Tumor". What did Ricky reckon it really was?
a: A misprint for "I Survived a 200 Pound Tuna"
x: A misprint for "I Survived a 200 Pound Turnip"
f: Ricky: "It was probably someone fell in the water and it came at him."
ex: Now, when are you ever in the mood to watch a TV show called "I survived a 200 pound tumor"?
Because it seems to me that you've got a 200 pound tumor you'll probably want to watch something else that'll take your mind off it Big Brother or whatever...
Well, I do I can't imagine what this is.
It must have been an error - 200 pound tumor?
It must have been a 200 pound tuna. It was probably someone fell in the water and it came at him.

q: Ricky turned up to XFM in agony, on the strongest painkillers he could get. How had he done his back in?
a: Wrestling a mate on their knees behind the couch
x: Lifting a crate of Rockbusters prizes
Stage diving at a Darkness gig
Falling off a bistro chair in Crouch End
f: It was a Friday night of wine and wrestling: "the last time, right, he sort of threw me... I went on my back and my back was done."
ex: Yeah. Well, we were wrestling. We were doing wrestling, right, in ff- the ff-- just behind the couch.
Yeah! Well, we were on our knees and then, sort of, like, ((incoherent)) ‘round, you know and I kept, I kept winning with an arm lock. Right?
And then the last time, right, he sort of threw me and I- on my- I went on my back and my back was done. And I was, you know. It was Iain Morris.

q: Karl argued that blind people get super hearing, so worms must too. Who did Ricky say you DON'T turn into just because you lose your eyes?
a: The Bionic Woman
f: Ricky: "You don't turn into Bionic Woman because you lose your eyes." Karl stuck to his guns: "If you use something a lot, you get better at it."
ex: So... you hear about this, don't you? You hear about, blind people have got really good ears.
And it's the same with a worm- no, they do, it's an extra sense, they-
No, it's not. That's nonsense, that's nonsense. They start getting used to relying on them more, but it doesn't- you don't turn into Bionic Woman because you lose your eyes.
No, but you do, because you use them more. If you use something a lot, you get better at it. So their ears are good. So all I'm saying is, so this rains coming down-

q: Karl said the shaking plant eventually picked out a caretaker as the murderer. Which cartoon did Ricky say never trusted the caretaker either?
a: Scooby Doo
f: Ricky: "Scooby Doo didn't like him from the beginning... why is that janitor so evil?"
ex: Was it an old man that- I mean, because Scooby Doo didn't like him from the beginning.
So, you know, why is that janitor so evil?

q: Ricky pictured the caretaker cracking under pressure from the plant. Which flower did he beg them to take away before confessing?
a: A chrysanthemum
f: Karl's defence: "Suddenly a plant grasses you up. You weren't expecting that." Ricky's caretaker: "Get that chrysanthemum away from me. I did it!"
ex: Well, no. It's one of them things, though. Imagine it. If you're that caretaker and you're thinking, "I've got away with this." Then suddenly a plant grasses you up. You weren't expecting that. So suddenly you're off guard
And you go, you go, "okay, okay, okay. Get that chrysanthemum away from me. I did it!" You're talking absolute bollocks. That was one of the most nonsense pieces of s*** I've ever heard in my life.
But anyway listen well it happened but,

q: Some builders on a tea break spotted Ricky in the street. What backhanded compliment did one of them give him?
a: "Not as fat as on telly"
f: Ricky took it to mean "you are fat, but you look even fatter on telly." He said all he could reply was "cheers, mate."
ex: Well, I was walking down the street and there's a group of builders sitting down having a cup of tea. One of them goes, alright, Rick? I went, alright, mate. The other one went, not as fat as on telly. I went, oh, thanks. Not as fat as on…

q: Making fun of the human-headed seagull, what did Ricky suggest the experiment could be for?
a: Saving on transport instead of getting a bus pass
x: Spying on people at the seaside
f: Ricky: "What is this, to save money on transport? Instead of getting a bus pass, you go, can I put my head on the seagull's body?"
ex: I'm not gonna get into argument about seagulls. It's all behind closed doors. How do you think we can change a, a heart now from another body? You have to try things out. It's trial and error. All sorts of weird stuff goes on in hospitals…

But what are they aiming towards when they're going to find out if you can put a head on a seagull's body? What are they want to learn and how do they want to apply that knowledge? A new heart is obviously for a reason. It saves a life.…

q: Ricky argued Karl's banana question was flawed. What did he suggest the London Zoo chimp might be given to eat instead?
a: One slice of banana, fifteen oranges, two hundred potatoes and some lettuce
x: Three pies, a Twix and a can of Tizer
Porridge, a boiled egg and toast soldiers
A melon, forty grapes and a Scotch egg
f: "It would eat fifteen if it was given fifteen!" Steve just wanted an answer: "How many bananas does it eat? Come on!" Ricky guessed five.
ex: But, hold on- but presumably they don't only feed it bananas...
So it's- so it's- so the question is--
It's "How many bananas does it eat?" Come on, Rick!
Yeah, but how many does it get given?! It would eat fifteen if it was given fifteen but it might be given, uh, one slice of banana, fifteen oranges, two hundred potatos and some lettuce!
How many bananas does it eat? Come on!

q: Ricky loved the look on Karl's face while he and Steve riffed on a Shakira lyric. What did he compare Karl to?
a: A cat looking back and forth between two people
x: A dog watching a tennis match
An owl spotting two mice at once
A goldfish following a ping-pong ball
f: Ricky: "you go 'pfhi-pfhi' to a cat and it looks back and forth between two people, that's very much like Karl was looking at us now."
ex: Karl... I love that look of Karl. Karl is looking back and forth, you know when you sort of, uh, you go "pfhi-pfhi" to a cat and it looks back and forth between two people, that's very much like Karl was looking at us now.

q: To show Karl what a virtual life could offer, what exciting new career did Ricky imagine for him?
a: A spy, briefed by MI5 about a Russian
x: An astronaut, sent to Mars by NASA
A striker, playing for Manchester United
A detective, hunting a jewel thief in Paris
f: Ricky's Karl: "Why was I hanging around with that bloke off The Office for? I'm a spy!" Karl's reply: "I prefer to leave everything as it is."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Philosophy · 2009
ex: In a minute you're going to be injected in the head, you're going to go to sleep, you're going to be in a flotation tank, but you are going to suddenly leave this office and it's going to be a virtual world. You can do what you want. You…
I prefer to leave everything as it is...
Go in it, but have everything the same so that I'm going "Hang on a minute! Has it actually happened?"

q: Ricky explained that he likes Robin partly because of his name. Which Robin did Ricky say he was like?
a: Robin off the Muppets
f: Ricky: "He's got little ways, Robin. That's why I like him. And it's because his name's Robin. Like Robin off the Muppets."
ex: Robin's not here anymore, but that's where he was sitting. He'd probably sit there again when he comes back. He's sort of like a creature of habit. When he comes around the flat, he always sits in the same little chair. He's got little…

q: Ricky said listening to Karl sell his futon (plum cover included) over the phone was like an episode of which TV show?
a: Changing Rooms
f: Karl even gave decorating tips: "I'll tell you what'll look nice in your spare bedroom…" Steve noted he did the deal in under 3 minutes.
ex: Uh- well- well he's- he's happy he likes the sound of it and I had a plum cover.
Yeah. Is Karl going, "That will go with (mumbles)" he's just going, "I'll tell you what'll look nice in your spare bedroom…" It was like a-
-an episode of Changing Rooms it was like listening to a representative Karl
He did the deal in under 3 minutes wasn't it?

q: Ricky ranted about people having fat "sliced off... and sucked out" under general anaesthetic. What did he want to tell them to do instead?
a: Just go for a run and stop eating burgers
x: Just eat salad and take the stairs
Just walk to work and skip pudding
f: Ricky's warning to them: "You might f***ing die!" Karl simply agreed: "I know."
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Medicine · 2008
ex: I don't know why, I really don't know why a doctor under Hippocratic Oath, takes the risk of something going badly wrong, sometimes general aesthetic because they can't be bothered to f***ing go for a run. Right? So they have f***ing bit…

q: Steve asked if Auntie Nora's new pills could explain why she "farted for 24 hours". How long did Ricky correct it to?
a: Five minutes
f: Karl blamed the medication: "that's what me mam said... Cause your body's in shock innit?"
s: The Ricky Gervais Guide to Medicine · 2008
ex: Could this be one of the reasons why she farted for 24 hours?
It could have been one of the side effects with it.

Yeah yeah, the that's, you know, that's what me mam said. It's all the medication. Cause your body's in shock innit? It has been, you know, given all these drugs that it's not used to. Ricky: Luckily some of the pills weren't…

q: As Karl started a Monkey News story about a struggling TV channel, what did Ricky vow?
a: To quit the show if one employee turned out to be a monkey doing a good job
x: To eat his hat if the story was true
To give Karl's wages to a zoo
To present the next show in a suit
f: Ricky: "If just one employee turns out to be simian and is doing a good job? I'm never doing this radio show again." Spoiler: the chimp did brilliantly.
ex: And they come in the next day and they were like, right, are we ready to go live? And that? And someone comes running with a clipboard saying, we haven't got any people left to present...
Right. I tell you what. All right, okay, carry on, carry on.
If just one employee turns out to be simian and is doing a good job? I'm never doing this radio show again.
So this TV channel, you know, it's having a lot of problems and that. They've got to go live, right? He's like, what am I gonna do? Anyway, for some reason, right, there was a chimp knocking about.

q: Zoe Ball was covering the slot while the show was off. Which DJ did Ricky say not to let in with her, because he "mixes up all the records"?
a: Big Boy Slim
f: Ricky's message for Zoe Ball: "Tell her not to get too comfortable", and don't let Big Boy Slim in, "cos he mixes up all the records doesn't he and ruins them."
ex: Yeah, Zoe Ball, who else is after her? She's not doing the whole run is she?
Is she doing the whole, the whole three months is she?
Tell her not to get too comfortable.
Alright. Don't let her feet... and don't let Big Boy Slim come in with her, cos he mixes up all the records doesn't he and ruins them.

q: During Karl's Room 101, Ricky slipped in a pet hate of his own. What was it?
a: People tutting at him in a narrow walkway when they're in the wrong
x: Staff who say 'have a nice day' and don't mean it
